summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, hypertension, dementia, and chronic pain presented with worsening head, neck, chest, and abdominal pain over one week. She and her son were concerned about a possible urinary tract infection recurrence due to prior associations between infections and pain flares, though no infection was found. She was treated with acetaminophen, IV fluids, and potassium supplementation. Her elevated lactate improved with hydration, hyponatremia resolved, and supratherapeutic INR was managed by holding warfarin with follow-up instructions. Imaging showed no acute intracranial, pulmonary, or abdominal pathology. Her pain improved significantly, and she was discharged home in stable condition with plans to resume warfarin after anticoagulation clinic follow-up.
